issue: Key correct. The writer's CHECK asked whether 91.9(a) reaches balloons when it names an 'Airplane or Rotorcraft Flight Manual'. It does: 91.9(a) applies to any 'civil aircraft', and its words 'or as otherwise prescribed by the certificating authority' cover a balloon's part 31 limitations. 31.81(b) requires them to be furnished in a Balloon Flight Manual or placard. The explanation also cited 31.81(a)(1) as if it named envelope temperature; it names only 'each operating limitation, including the maximum weight'.
suggested: CHECK removed, explanation reworded to cite 31.81 accurately, ref changed to '14 CFR 91.9(a); 14 CFR 31.81', confidence set to high. (Applied in pilot-4.json.)

issue: Key correct. Current 91.147(a), last amended at 89 FR 33108 (Apr. 26, 2024, which added the part 5 SMS item), limits 'Operator' to airplanes, powered-lift and rotorcraft. 136.1(c) excludes balloons, and 120.1(a) reaches only operators 'as defined in 14 CFR 91.147'. Federal Register API searches (FAA rules and proposed rules since 2023-01-01 for balloon + drug/alcohol, balloon tour, commercial balloon, and '91.147') found no rule adding balloons; the only 2026 item naming 91.147 is a petition for a weight-shift sightseeing exemption (2026-19562). The CHECK's unsourced claim that 'the NTSB has recommended drug and alcohol testing for commercial balloon operators' could not be verified. The key also left out 'nonstop', a defining element of a 91.147 Operator.
suggested: CHECK removed (resolved). The unverified NTSB claim is dropped. The key now reads 'A nonstop sightseeing operator for hire in an airplane, powered-lift or rotorcraft.' Distractors reworded to similar length. Confidence set to high. (Applied in pilot-4.json.)
